plans.objective: [DIM: composition] The rigid family corresponds to functions expressible in a fixed low-dimensional basis (e.g., degree-d monomials), while the fat family corresponds to high-degree random polynomial expansions with unbounded coefficient space.

steps.description: Implement the `family` function to generate training and held-out constraint points for two function classes: (1) Rigid family — low-degree monomials (degree-d) with fixed basis, ensuring low-dimensional solution space; (2) Fat family — high-degree random polynomial expansions with unbounded coefficient space. Ensure all outputs are (N,1)-shaped arrays, held-out points do not overlap with training points, and y/yv are normalized to O(1) scale (std ≲ 10) to make the 1e-3 zero-violation criterion meaningful. This is the only function to be implemented per the script contract; the capacity_scan infrastructure will handle width scanning, optimization, and N_c determination.

plans.objective: ** [DIM: structure] The rigid family corresponds to functions whose graph lies on a low-dimensional algebraic variety (codimension > 0 in the input-output space), whereas the fat family spans a volume-filling set where no non-trivial polynomial constraint vanishes on all members.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the family function for the rigid and fat families according to the hypothesis. The rigid family should be functions on a low-dimensional algebraic variety (e.g., a polynomial of fixed degree), while the fat family should be volume-filling (e.g., high-degree random polynomials). Ensure proper normalization (std ≲ 10), correct shape (N,1), and non-overlapping training/holdout sets. This is the core implementation needed to test the bootstrap rigidity hypothesis.

plans.objective: ** [DIM: structure] The rigid family corresponds to functions that satisfy a specific second-order linear elliptic PDE (e.g., Laplace or Helmholtz equation) on the domain, imposing a smoothness constraint that reduces the effective solution space, whereas the fat family consists of functions that do not satisfy any such local differential constraint.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the `family` function to generate training/holdout data for the "rigid" family (functions satisfying Helmholtz equation Δu + k²u = 0, e.g., sin(kx) on [0, π]) and the "fat" family (high-degree random polynomials, e.g., degree-19 random basis (2z-1)^19). Ensure y/yv are normalized to O(1) scale, Xv and X are non-overlapping, and outputs are reshaped to (N,1). This enables the capacity_scan to properly probe the rigidity hypothesis.
